tldr_label: TL;DR — Democrats win both chambers of Congress in a rebuke to Trump; Texas, Kansas and Maine flip

tldr_bullets.label: Congress
tldr_bullets.body: Major outlets project that Democrats won both the House and the Senate. CBS News called the result a rebuke of President Trump. Some races, including Alaska's Senate seat, remain uncalled. [[TAG:success:Dems win Congress]]

tldr_bullets.label: Key races
tldr_bullets.body: Democrats won Senate seats in Texas, Maine, Iowa, Kansas and Michigan. Gina Hinojosa unseated Texas Governor Greg Abbott.

tldr_bullets.label: Trump
tldr_bullets.body: Trump said he accepts the results and congratulated Democrats, while blaming Republican candidates for the losses.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: Futures first fell sharply, then recovered after Trump accepted the results. The dollar weakened, and Brent traded near $104. [[TAG:warning:volatile open]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Iran called the US reply on Hormuz 'unconvincing' after the Qeshm strikes. Trump told the FT there are no immediate plans to strike Iran.

tldr_bullets.label: World
tldr_bullets.body: Israel's president opens coalition consultations today, and South Africans vote in local elections. The toll from the Russian strike in Zaporizhzhia region has risen to 31, according to Al Jazeera. [[TAG:danger:31 killed]]

sections.title: Democrats Take Congress
sections.summary: Democrats win the House and Senate in what CBS calls a rebuke of Trump; some races uncalled

paragraphs.heading: The result
paragraphs.body: CBS News, CNN and NPR, citing projections and AP race calls, reported that Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate. Republicans had held the Senate 53-47 and a narrow House majority. NBC News reported that Democrats won the House majority, but seat totals are still changing as races are called. [[TAG:success:both chambers]]

paragraphs.heading: Senate flips
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that Democrats clinched the Senate. CBS News and CNBC said Democrats flipped seats in Maine, Ohio, North Carolina, South Carolina, Iowa and Kansas. Axios and NPR reported that Abdul El-Sayed beat Mike Rogers in Michigan and becomes the first Muslim elected to the Senate. Alaska remained too close to call in NBC's tracker. [[TAG:warning:Alaska uncalled]]

paragraphs.heading: Texas
paragraphs.body: KUT and Houston Public Media reported that James Talarico beat Ken Paxton for the Senate, ending a three-decade Republican run of statewide wins in Texas, and that Gina Hinojosa unseated Governor Greg Abbott. In Florida, The Washington Post reported that Republican Byron Donalds won the governor's race.

sections.sources: CBS News, CNN, NPR, NBC News, CNBC, Axios, KUT, Houston Public Media, Washington Post

sections.title: Reaction
sections.summary: Trump accepts the results and blames GOP candidates; leaders abroad read a change of course

paragraphs.heading: Trump
paragraphs.body: Forbes reported that Trump congratulated Democrats and said he accepts the results. RTE said he deflected blame onto Republican candidates. CNN reported his acceptance, which settles for now questions about whether he would challenge the outcome.

paragraphs.heading: Abroad
paragraphs.body: Reuters, via US News, gathered international reactions. Spain's Pedro Sánchez and Norway's Jonas Gahr Støre welcomed the result, South Africa's Cyril Ramaphosa spoke of a new era, Russia's deputy foreign minister urged waiting for final results, and Japan said its alliance with the US remains the cornerstone of its security.

sections.title: Markets
sections.summary: Futures swing, then steady as Trump accepts the results; dollar dips and Brent nears $104

paragraphs.heading: Election Day close
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that the S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92, ending a three-day losing streak as chip stocks rebounded. The Nasdaq gained 0.83% and the Dow fell 0.38%.

paragraphs.heading: Overnight reaction
paragraphs.body: The Globe and Mail, citing Reuters, reported that Nasdaq-100 futures fell as much as 2.4% before recovering after Trump accepted the results, and that the dollar weakened. Yahoo Finance said futures fell after Democrats took both chambers. AOL reported a later rally. Fox Business described futures as mixed. Moves vary by time of report. [[TAG:warning:volatile]]

paragraphs.heading: Oil
paragraphs.body: FinanceFeeds reported that Brent settled on Tuesday at its lowest level since early October, near $104. NBC News called Monday's slide the biggest drop since July. Arab News reported that oil rose after the election on uncertainty over the Iran war.

sections.title: Iran
sections.summary: Tehran calls the US reply on Hormuz 'unconvincing' after the Qeshm strikes

paragraphs.heading: Talks stall
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Iran called the US reply to its plan to reopen Hormuz 'unconvincing' and that Trump confirmed the strikes on Qeshm. The Jerusalem Post said Iran and the US remain far from a deal and that Tehran has threatened to respond to the strikes. NBC News and CBS News described the US strikes as limited. Qatar says both sides remain committed to talks. [[TAG:warning:far from deal]]

sections.title: Israel
sections.summary: Herzog opens consultations as the opposition unites behind Eisenkot

paragraphs.heading: Consultations
paragraphs.body: TRT World reported that the opposition is rallying behind Eisenkot as Herzog opens consultations on the next government. The Jerusalem Post reported that Naftali Bennett's party will recommend him. The Times of Israel reported that Eisenkot vowed to use the Knesset majority quickly against what he called the 'Oct. 7 government'. The Jerusalem Post said the haredi parties remain the key to any coalition. The first mandate holder gets 28 days, which can be extended. [[TAG:info:mandate pending]]

sections.title: Ukraine
sections.summary: Zaporizhzhia aid-center toll rises to 31 as Russia confirms talks in Abu Dhabi

paragraphs.heading: Toll and talks
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera put the toll from Russia's strike on an aid hub in Zaporizhzhia region at 31, up from earlier counts of 24 to 26. CNBC reported that Russia confirmed peace talks in Abu Dhabi next week and signaled a possible summit of Trump, Putin and Xi. Ukrinform reported that Ukraine downed most of about 310 drones launched overnight. [[TAG:danger:31 killed]]

sections.summary: Belgium's king consults party leaders; South Africa votes in a test for the ANC

paragraphs.heading: Belgium
paragraphs.body: Anadolu, via aNews, reported that King Philippe began talks with party leaders after Prime Minister Bart De Wever submitted his resignation over the budget. The king has not yet accepted it.
